jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Moving Backward
jokes.joke: My girlfriend said she needed to move on, and two weeks later she started dating a Civil War reenactor. I didn’t take it well. Not because she found someone else—because apparently “moving on” meant 1863. I got replaced by a guy who spends every Saturday losing the same war on purpose.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Closure at the Pet Store
jokes.joke: My ex texted me a picture of her new boyfriend. Then, an hour later, a picture of a puppy they just adopted together. I don't know which one hurt worse, but I did notice the puppy looked more excited to be there. So I went to a pet store, just to feel wanted by something with a heartbeat. Guy asks, 'Can I help you?' I said, 'Depends. Do any of these hamsters know how to commit?'

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Declaration of Separation
jokes.joke: My ex moved on and is now dating a historical reenactor. It’s impossible to compete with that kind of confidence. I called her to ask for my favorite hoodie back, and this guy picked up the phone in full character to inform me that the colonies had declared independence and my tea was in the harbor.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Ex at the Pet Store
jokes.joke: I ran into my ex at the pet store last week. She's moving on—she was adopting a cat. I watched her for a second and thought, yeah, that tracks. Finally found a living thing that will ignore her the exact same way I did.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Pet Store Rebound
jokes.joke: I realized my ex had fully moved on when the pet store clerk greeted me with, “Oh, you’re the guy she used to date.” She’s in there every week buying new toys for her dog, and I’m just standing there thinking, “Great, even her pets have a more stable relationship than I do.”

scores.comment: Clear first-person bit with a solid escalation, but the hamster 'commit' punchline is a familiar relationship-wordplay turn rather than a strong surprise.
Strong premise, economical escalation, and a vivid final image. The independence/tea payoff lands cleanly and carries the joke.
Tight and stage-ready, with a clean reversal, though the joke about cats ignoring people is familiar enough to limit surprise and originality.
Competent and understandable, but the final comparison about pets having a more stable relationship is predictable and does not sharpen into a strong punchline.
